top_choice_rationale: P002 credits Katori and Ye for the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and its realisation at the 10^-18 level. The idea is specific, rests on atomic structure (differential polarizabilities, blackbody and lattice shifts) that can be checked inside the field, and has been confirmed by independent laboratories and species over about two decades. The two-name credit splits cleanly into concept and demonstration, and the citation can be centred on the many-atom magic-wavelength lattice so it stays distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. The record accuracy figures and the Lemonde/Ludlow/PTB/NIST/SYRTE credit edge still need checking. P001 follows as a clean prediction-then-observation result of new moire quantum matter, but its pairing mechanism, disorder sensitivity and experimental credit beyond three names are still moving. P003 is mature but the credit among Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, Cirac and Jaksch is soft and it sits close to earlier prizes. Any award is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: Possible recusal on P002: Kroll spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, linked to the JILA precision-spectroscopy environment of Jun Ye, with no documented collaboration with Katori or Ye. He is also professionally close to precision spectroscopy as a Lund atomic physicist. For P003 his European quantum-memory collaborations overlap the Cirac/Zoller community.
